summary: Wrote MYCELIUM_NETWORK_SPEC.md — the Layer 3 spec of record, which discharges decision D-04 (Layer 3 is not built until its spec exists). Grounded first by reading the fleet doctrine — MYCELIUM.md, HEARTH_SPEC.md, HEARTWOOD.md — so the wallet's spec uses the established vocabulary (the five identity layers, mycorrhizal partnerships, the hyphal lattice, anchoring rings, forest consensus) rather than reinventing it. The spec captures the operator's People-network vision plus the two design decisions the operator made via chips: D-09, graded verification tiers — every connection carries a signed leaf saying how it was verified, Tier R remote / Tier P in-person handshake / Tier V device-verified presence (biometric + geolocation + timestamp); and D-10, organizations as first-class network entities that issue nested membership attestations, with proof-of-place working through membership rather than through an engineered residency-proof feature. Sixteen sections, a 5a-5e build phasing, and an honest treatment of the three hard problems — sybil resistance, social-graph privacy, and the real meaning of 'the whole world in your tree'. Decisions D-09 and D-10 recorded in decisions.md; PLAN.md Phase 5 updated to point at the now-existing spec.

why.text: Operator: 'Let's do the spec.' The operator asked for a tight set of chips — only the decisions genuinely needed — answered two (verification tiers, proof-of-place), and asked the Carpenter to design the doc. D-04 required this spec before any Layer 3 code; writing it unblocks Phase 5. Grounded per the grounding-gate hook: the three fleet doctrine docs were read before drafting so the spec is consistent, not a reinvention.

outcome.notes: [P-001] MYCELIUM_NETWORK_SPEC.md written, discharges D-04. [P-002] D-09 and D-10 recorded. [P-003] PLAN.md Phase 5 updated; first build slice is Phase 5a, the in-person handshake. [FEEDBACK->Foreman]: no notes — the chip-then-design rhythm the operator asked for worked cleanly; two decisions were genuinely needed and the rest derived from doctrine.

uncertainty: A spec is a design draft, not running code — its real test is the build. The operator's two chip answers were rich and somewhat expanded scope (organizations moved from 'deferred' to core); the spec interprets them faithfully but the operator should read it and correct any misread before Phase 5a is cut. Tier V device-verified presence depends on biometric/geolocation capabilities whose feasibility in an iOS PWA is an open question flagged in the spec.
next: Operator reviews MYCELIUM_NETWORK_SPEC.md and corrects any misread. Then cut Phase 5a — the in-person QR/NFC handshake, local only, no networking — the smallest useful slice of Layer 3, reusing the Phase 2.6 in-person co-sign primitives and the relationship attestation kind.
